label: Capability promised at announcement materially under-delivered or never shipped
description: A manufacturer publicly commits to a specific capability (range, top speed, accessory, software feature) at product announcement and either delivers a substantially lesser version, or never ships the promised feature at all. Pre-orders, deposits, and purchase decisions are made on the basis of the announcement, not the delivered reality.
regulatory_basis: FTC Act §5 (deceptive acts in commerce). State consumer-protection statutes vary; some states' UDAP laws explicitly cover failure to deliver advertised features. Class actions on this pattern are common (e.g., Tesla FSD class actions, Cybertruck range extender refunds).
consumer_harm: Buyers commit to a product (often with non-refundable deposits) on the basis of promised capability and discover post-purchase that the capability is unavailable. Unlike traditional deception, the promise was made in good faith at the time but engineering or business decisions invalidated it later.
